title: HelperSessionSpawnParams
description: Params of the helper session service's spawn op: start a shell under a new PTY on the host. There is NO command and NO argv here, and that is the shape being frozen rather than an omission — the host's registration path refuses any op whose params carry a free-form string list, because an input reaches a command line. Which shell runs is the helper's composition-root decision (its login-shell resolution), so a remote caller names the environment a session starts in and never the program it starts.

cwd.description: Where the shell starts. Empty means the helper's own default, which is the user's home — the same resolution internal/pty already makes, rather than a second answer to one question. The RESOLVED directory comes back in the launch record.

env.description: Additional environment entries, as a MAP rather than the string slice exec wants. Not only because the registration rule refuses the slice: a map cannot express a positional argument, so no caller can smuggle argv through it, and a duplicate key is impossible rather than last-wins.

windowBytes.description: The requested bound on this session's output window. The coordinator decides and the helper applies, clamped to the helper's own floor, ceiling and aggregate budget — the cost is spent on somebody else's machine, so the helper keeps the last word. 0 means the helper's default. What the session actually got is reported back in the launch record, because a silently ignored setting is the degrade the product must never hide.
